equivalent_not_counted.rule: dirs: empty XDG_DATA_DIRS elements are skipped
equivalent_not_counted.argument: The mutant keeps the empty element and appends the literal directory '/mime/' (d + '/mime/' with d = ''). The only way that changes an answer is if a database exists under /mime; the case schema materialises files only below {root}, and /mime does not exist on the measurement host (tested: `test -d /mime` false), so the extra directory is inert. Order of the real directories is unchanged, so no case can distinguish it. Measured: identical (type, uncertain) on all 55 cases.

equivalent_not_counted.rule: mode: a dir with a valid cache does not also read its globs
equivalent_not_counted.argument: Without the `continue`, a dir with a valid mime.cache also parses its globs2 into TextDB. TextDB is only consulted when `caches` is empty (`self.db = CacheDB(caches) if caches else text`), and a dir that produced a cache guarantees `caches` is non-empty; `self.mode` is computed from the same list. The extra parse therefore cannot reach any answer. Measured: identical on all 55 cases, including mode-06-cache-ignores-globs (cache + globs2 in one dir).

equivalent_not_counted.rule: text: fgets line chunks are at most 254 bytes (newline search window)
equivalent_not_counted.argument:
The 255-byte window differs only when a '
' sits at exactly offset 254 of a chunk: the 254-window then ends the chunk before it (end = i+254) and the next chunk is the bare '
'; the 255-window ends the chunk after it (end = nl+1 = i+255). Both parse to the same globs, because a chunk ending in '
' has that byte stripped and a one-byte '
' chunk is neither a comment nor a ':' line, so it is skipped, and the following chunk starts at the same byte in both models. Measured: identical (type, uncertain) for newline offsets 240..265 in a 400-byte line, over 4 names (eq harness, 26 fixtures). fgets-02 (the 254-byte chunk end) IS killed by fgets-01-chunk-254, so the chunk length itself stays covered.

equivalent_not_counted.rule: text: a chunk starting with NUL is skipped
equivalent_not_counted.argument: A chunk whose first byte is NUL is truncated to b'' by `line = chunk.split(b'\0', 1)[0]`, then fails `k = p.find(b':') < 0` and is skipped, exactly as the explicit NUL test would do. The mutation only removes an early exit, not a parse. Measured: identical on NUL bytes at offsets 0, 1, 253, 254, 255, 508 of a globs2 file (eq harness, 6 fixtures, 2 names each) and on all 55 cases.
